01 · About me

A background
across borders.

An engineering education in Japan. A new chapter in Ningbo.

I am Tingyi Li, a postgraduate student in Electronic Communication and Computer Engineering at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China. Before this, I studied Electronic Engineering and Computer Science at Tokyo Metropolitan University.

My undergraduate project brought electronics and programming together through the visualization of MOSFET operating regions. I am now exploring where to take my interests next, including possible doctoral study.

Studying in Japan gave me experience learning and communicating in another language. I use Chinese as my native language, communicate comfortably in Japanese, and continue my studies in English.

Home/Research

04 · Undergraduate research

A closer look
inside a circuit.

Tokyo Metropolitan University · Graduation project

Visualization of Transistor Operating Regions and Its Applications

I developed an analysis program that converts circuit simulation data into a visual account of MOSFET behavior, highlighting differences between healthy and faulty circuits.

LTspiceMOSFETData visualizationFault analysis
Explore methods & results ↗

The question

How can transistor operating regions help reveal changes inside a faulty circuit, beyond comparing output waveforms?

The approach

Classify each transistor as cutoff, linear or saturation over time, then visualize the intervals in which healthy and faulty circuits differ.

Home/Research/Methods & results

Research details

From simulation
to visible differences.

A closer look at the method and selected figures from my undergraduate thesis.

3Circuit types4Fault conditions3Operating regions
01 · Prepare

Read LTspice .raw output with RawRead and export time and node-voltage data to CSV.

02 · Classify

Extract model threshold parameters and classify each MOSFET using its gate, drain and source voltages.

03 · Compare

Align healthy and faulty time series, isolate differing operating-region intervals and export comparison figures.

Evaluation setup

A 2-to-4 decoder, a half adder and a majority circuit were simulated using transient analysis, with input signals varying between 0 V and a 1.2 V supply.

Fault conditions

A +50 mV NMOS threshold shift; NMOS channel width reduced by half; supply IR drop modeled with a 50 Ω resistor; and an open circuit modeled with a 1 TΩ resistor.

Selected results.

Original plots for the majority circuit. Click either figure to enlarge. The colours identify operating regions, not fault severity.

CutoffLinearSaturation

Findings and scope

In these simulations, local faults tended to produce concentrated differences, while supply degradation produced more distributed patterns. The method supports inspection of fault effects and their propagation. It does not provide automatic fault diagnosis, and small changes that do not cross region boundaries may be missed. Results depend on simulation models and conditions; physical circuits require further validation.

Source: my undergraduate thesis, “トランジスタの動作領域可視化とその応用,” pp. 1–5. Original figures 9 and 12 are from p. 3.
